description: Common hotspot classes, the profiler evidence that identifies them, and the optimization families most likely to pay off. Use during Phase 2 profiling and backlog replenishment.

hotspot_classes.evidence: cProfile/line_profiler shows one Python/R loop dominating; high pct in a single function with primitive ops
runtime scales superlinearly with input size; list.count/index/in or repeated concatenation in a loop
tracemalloc/Massif/heaptrack shows high allocation counts or large transient peaks; RSS far above steady working set
same file/schema/metadata parsed many times; IO or parse functions high in cumulative time across calls
/usr/bin/time -v shows low %CPU and high system time; many small reads/writes/flushes
import/startup exceeds 50% of runtime at the per-iteration size
hotspot_classes.note: Also a signal to INCREASE the per-iteration benchmark size; startup-only wins do not scale.

hotspot_classes.evidence: low CPU utilization on a multi-core machine; embarrassingly parallel structure in profiles
compiled artifacts built with -O0/debug; no vectorization reports; debug symbols in production path
mostly-zero data materialized dense; memory jumps at a conversion call site
serialize->deserialize between in-process stages; marshal/pickle/json high in profile
